public_payload.normalized_proposition: Marcus reaffirms as still true his February 2023 summary that ChatGPT, the world's most used chatbot, is governed by undisclosed training data and a barely described algorithm, is glorified by the media, and has ethical guardrails that only sorta kinda work and are driven more by text similarity than by any true moral calculus.

statement.excerpt: So, to sum up, we now have the world’s most used chatbot, governed by training data that nobody knows about, obeying an algorithm that is only hinted at, glorified by the media, and yet with ethical guardrails that only sorta kinda work and that are driven more by text similarity than any true moral calculus.

our_interpretation: The October 2024 reaffirmation concerns the contemporary ChatGPT service, rather than only its February 2023 version.

For this ongoing observation, the target reporting period is September 2024, the last complete calendar month before publication. Earlier studies provide context, not direct measurements of that period.
An ordinary reading of the disclosure criticism is that outsiders lack detailed training-data and implementation information, not that nobody inside OpenAI knows it.
An ordinary reading of incomplete guardrails is that adversarial prompts can sometimes elicit prohibited responses. It does not mean every safeguard fails.
Website traffic is a partial measure of usage; it does not establish a ranking across applications, embedded assistants and unique users.
The comparison between text similarity and moral calculus is a separate claim about mechanism. Successful jailbreaks alone cannot establish it.
Media glorification means broadly favorable or inflated treatment, rather than simply extensive coverage.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable usage measurements establish leadership; technical records establish limited disclosure; relevant evaluations demonstrate guardrail failures; and independent evidence establishes the claimed media treatment and predominance of text similarity in safety decisions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes that a material component is false, such as another chatbot leading usage, sufficiently complete public technical disclosures, or controlled evidence against the claimed safety mechanism. Isolated successful refusals do not contradict the claim that guardrails work incompletely.

evidence.locator: Opening paragraph beneath the repeated article title
evidence.explanation: Supports usage leadership on the reported worldwide desktop and mobile website-visit measure. It does not establish leadership by unique users across every interface.

evidence.excerpt: On one of our hardest jailbreaking tests, GPT‑4o scored 22 (on a scale of 0-100) while our o1‑preview model scored 84.
evidence.explanation: The company reports incomplete jailbreak resistance, supporting that component of Marcus's description. The same announcement describes improved resistance and contextual reasoning about safety rules, which complicates a uniform characterization of ChatGPT's safeguards.

evidence.excerpt: We found that in terms of the text modality, GPT-4o exhibits stronger safety compared to GPT-4V.
evidence.explanation: The experiments report successful attacks alongside improved text safety and ineffective attack methods. They establish that both vulnerabilities and functioning defenses existed, but do not measure September deployments or distinguish text similarity from moral reasoning.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A September 2024 disclosure inventory and representative media study, together with controlled evidence testing an explicitly defined similarity-versus-reasoning distinction and comparable usage measurements across interfaces.
